contract.json_path: Flat body worked (no `exploratory_session` wrapper needed) — invokeCapability builds /exploratory_session/* itself from each field's declared json_path, matching describeCapability's guidance verbatim.

notes: CREATED SESSION FOR DEPENDENT PROBES — session_id (integer, use this) = 779, identifier = ES-14 (display only; per get_exploratory_session's own guidance the identifier fails routing as a 404, so the six gated capabilities must be called with the integer 779), project_id = 379335744 (PR-2005), folder_id requested = 764138 (__scratch__), session_state = 'active', session_log_count = 0 at creation (so a clone probe should hit clone_exploratory_session's SYNCHRONOUS path per its own guidance — the async threshold is 50+ logs). owner/assignee were left unset in this probe (untested) — if update/close probes want to exercise ownership they need a valid TCM owner id first. DRIFT #1 (declared_missing): folder_id is a declared property of the 201 response schema (and of get_exploratory_session's return list) but the key is completely ABSENT — not null, just missing — from both the create response and a follow-up get_exploratory_session(project_id=379335744, session_id=779) read-back (200, body identical in every other respect). So it is unverifiable from the API surface whether the session actually landed in folder 764138 (__scratch__) or at the project root; a caller cannot confirm folder placement through this capability's own response or through get_exploratory_session. DRIFT #2 (value-level, not required/json_path but worth flagging for the other six probes): `charter` was sent as a non-empty string ('Verify create_exploratory_session contract end to end.') and came back `null` on both the create response AND the read-back — the field is silently dropped on create despite being declared writable with its own json_path (distinct from the already-documented 'cloning does not copy charter' behavior — this is create itself losing it). Anything relying on charter being set at creation time should instead set it via update_exploratory_session and re-verify. Error envelope: confirmed the family's known defect — a deliberate 404 (nonexistent project_id) returned bare {"success":false} with no `error` object, against the declared {success:false,error:{code,message,details}} schema; per instructions this was NOT diffed into declared_missing/undeclared_returned (no 200 was involved), only called out here. Entitlement-gate check: not applicable/not observed — the error path returned a proper 404 status, not a 200 {success:false}, so no evidence of the 2xx-masking-refusal product defect on this capability. Container check: response correctly nested under `exploratory_session` with no `data` wrapper, matching the declared shape — no container mismatch here. Minor quirk: `project_id` (undeclared in the response schema either way) comes back as a STRING ("379335744") on the create response but as an INTEGER (379335744) on the get_exploratory_session read-back of the same session — inconsistent typing between the two endpoints for an undeclared field, noted for awareness only since it's not part of the declared contract. Guidance for the six gated capabilities: session is currently ACTIVE with 0 logs and no issues/attachments/configurations/tags — a clean starting state. Whether close_exploratory_session subsequently blocks update/log edits is UNKNOWN and should be tested by probing update/log-create/clone before close_exploratory_session, then confirming afterward whether edits on a closed session are rejected — recommend running close last among the six so the other five aren't stranded if closing does lock the session.
